research.line: Tele-MANAS, the Government of India national tele-mental-health helpline
research.official_name: Tele MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States), the National Tele Mental Health Programme (NTMHP) of India. Hindi on the official site: टेली मानस. Official texts write it three ways: "Tele MANAS", "Tele-MANAS" and "TELE Manas".
research.run_by: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India, under the National Health Mission. NIMHANS in Bengaluru is the apex nodal centre and IIIT-Bangalore is the technology partner. NHSRC gives health-systems support. Five regional coordinating centres back it (NIMHANS, LGBRIMH Tezpur, CIP Ranchi, IHBAS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh), plus 23 mentoring institutes. State and UT Tele MANAS cells answer the calls: 53 cells across 36 States/UTs as of February 2026 and June 2026.

facts.value: Tele MANAS stands for Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States. It is the National Tele Mental Health Programme and the digital arm of the District Mental Health Programme. (The FAQ's expansion inserts 'the' before Networking.)
facts.quote: Tele MANAS is the National Tele Mental Health Programme. It stands for Tele Mental Health Assistance and the Networking Across States (Tele MANAS).

facts.topic: run by / how a call works
facts.value: Calls go to the Tele MANAS cell of the caller's state or UT. Counsellors answer by region and by the caller's chosen language, and refer on to specialists when needed.
facts.quote: The calls would be routed to Tele MANAS cells in the respective state and union territory, where the call will be answered by trained counsellors based on your region and corresponding choice of language

facts.value: Calls start with an automated voice menu (IVRS), audio only, and use an auto-callback. A caller may be called back rather than answered live.
facts.quote: This call will be an IVRS based audio calling only, with a timely auto-call back approach. Through the automated callback service, the caller will first be attended to by a trained counsellor.

facts.value: Open 24/7 and free
facts.quote: Tele MANAS is a 24/7 on-demand service available free of cost with ease of access via phone calls

facts.value: Still described as a 24x7 toll-free helpline giving free tele-counselling (Feb 2026)
facts.quote: Provides free tele-counseling for mental health, with call escalations for more specialised interventions through psychiatrists, clinical psychologists, psychiatric social workers and psychiatric nurses.

facts.value: Open to any individual, with no sex restriction stated. Family members and ASHAs or community volunteers may also call on someone's behalf.
facts.quote: Any individual with mental health issues can reach out to Tele MANAS services for help. 2. Family members of persons with mental health issues can reach out for help.

facts.value: The Union Health Minister said men and women call in almost equal numbers (World Mental Health Day 2025)
facts.quote: The almost equal number of men and women seeking help demonstrates that awareness is growing among all groups.

facts.value: No age limit is stated in any official text read. The service supports parents and carers of children and adolescents. The Education Ministry (Feb 2024) and CBSE (Aug 2025) promote it to school students. It is not adults-only.
facts.quote: students can call at any time for free and confidential support

facts.value: 20 languages, set by what each state opted for. Hindi and English are the first two in the only itemised official list found (PIB, 7 Feb 2023).
facts.quote: At present, the Tele-MANAS services are available in 20 languages based on languages opted by states: Hindi, English, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Konkani, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Bengali, Odia, Punjabi, Kashmiri, Bodo, Dogri, Urdu, Manipuri, Mizo and Rajasthani.

fit.chapter_topic: Station (1971 railway world; the family's electrical shop on the station road): an applicant complained about a past boss bullying the workers (the man), and in the twin she reported her last boss for bullying the staff (the woman). Title card: a complaint of bullying at work.
fit.why: It fits for talking to someone, not for making a complaint. For: the official site (assets/i18n/en.json) lists "workplace stress" among the day-to-day challenges it covers. It says the programme's vision includes "those who are facing day-to-day challenges in their personal, professional, and social life". The Oct 2026 PIB release counts "stress related to examinations, workplaces and relationships" among what callers raise. Against: the official FAQ lists only "Tele Counselling by trained counsellors", tele-consultation and "Referral Services to other Mental Health Establishments". It does not take, investigate or act on a bullying complaint. The words "bullying" and "harassment" appear in none of the official Tele-MANAS text I fetched. The FAQ also frames callers as people "with mental health issues", which a bullied worker may not see as being about them. So a player who is being bullied now, or punished for complaining, gets support but no remedy. The "?" sheet should offer it as someone to talk to, not as a place to report. No better line: I found no official text for any national line that takes workplace-bullying complaints from women and men alike. One search found no Ministry of Labour line for this.

research.line: ERSS 112 (Emergency Response Support System), India's single national emergency number
research.official_name: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), number 112. It also appears as "ERSS-112" and "Dial 112", and MHA's slogan is "One India One Emergency Number 112". In Hindi, PIB (24 Nov 2025) calls it "आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया सहायता प्रणाली (ई आर एस एस)". A 2023 PIB Hindi release writes it out as "इमर्जेंसी रीस्पान्स सपोर्ट सिस्टम (ईआरएसएस) 112".
research.run_by: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India, runs it through the Women Safety Division's Safe City Project/ERSS Section, with money from the Nirbhaya Fund. Each State and UT runs its own part: its own Emergency Response Centre or Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP), usually led by the state police. C-DAC developed the software, and the 112.gov.in footer reads "© C-DAC".

fit.chapter_topic: Lugdi (a ghat road at night): reports of being followed at night
fit.why: This is the case 112 exists for. The 112.gov.in 'When to use' page (archived 20 Apr 2026) says to trigger SOS "when you feel your safety or the safety of another is in imminent danger". Its category list includes 'Need Police' and 'Women Safety', and the FAQ lists being "the victim or witness of an aggression or fight" as a time you can call. It serves citizens of any gender, so it fits both halves. Adversarial catch for the man's half: the app's SHOUT feature, which alerts nearby volunteers, is offered only "In case of women and children" (112.gov.in home, archived 12 May 2026). So the sheet should show the number 112 and not promise SHOUT.

fit.chapter_topic: Jadugar (a travelling magic show): harassment reports backstage
fit.why: In the chapter, a man from the audience followed a dancer backstage and the fair's officials want a statement, so the harassment is being reported after it happened. 112 fits only while the danger is live, while someone is still being followed or threatened. For non-urgent matters the official 112 FAQ points people to the local police instead. 112 is not a line for filing a harassment report or making a statement. I found no national line that serves women and men alike for harassment at work. SHe-Box is for women only: the PIB doc of 29 Mar 2025 calls it a platform "for women to register workplace sexual harassment complaints". 181 is also for women only. NALSA 15100 does not serve both alike either: its eligibility list names "Women and Children" outright, while men qualify only through other categories or an income limit. 112 is still the only official national line that serves both halves, if the sheet frames it as 'if you or someone is in danger right now'.

fit.chapter_topic: Cricket (a cricket ground): police complaints of violence at home
fit.why: For violence happening now, 112 fits both halves. It dispatches police, and the FAQ lists "When you are the victim or witness of an aggression or fight." as a time to call. But the chapter's lines are about complaints already filed ('Faces a police complaint for violence at home', 'A neighbour's police complaint says violence at home'). Following up a complaint after the fact is local police station work, and the 112 FAQ steers non-urgent matters to the local police. The obvious alternative, Women Helpline 181, fails the owner's rule. PIB (29 Mar 2025) says it serves "women facing violence in both public and private spaces", which is women only. The same PIB doc also says 181 is unified under 112. NALSA 15100 legal aid is not symmetric (see the Jadugar entry). No better line serves women and men alike.

fit.notes:
Verdict: keep 112 for all three chapters. It is the only official national line I found that serves women and men alike, it is current, and it answers in Hindi and English. Two chapters need careful wording on the '?' sheet. In Jadugar and Cricket the situations are reports and complaints made after the fact, but 112 is for danger right now. Suggested framing: 'In danger right now? Call 112.' Do not present it as a place to file a complaint, and do not mention SHOUT, which is offered only to women and children.

Things I tried to break the plan with and what came back:
(a) Replaced or merged? No. 112 is the number that absorbs the others: 100, 101, 108 and 181 are being integrated into it (112.gov.in About, PIB 2025).
(b) Women or children only? No. Every official description says citizens or persons in distress. The Nirbhaya Fund branding ('for ensuring safety of women and children') and the MIB 2020 advisory ('for enhanced safety of women') are framing only; the service itself is not limited to women.
(c) Language: the FAQ says to speak the state language, with English/Hindi available in 36 states/UTs.

Reliability flags:
(1) The live 112.gov.in timed out from this network, so the language and when-to-use quotes rest on raw Wayback id_ copies from Dec 2025 to May 2026. Re-open https://112.gov.in/faq from an Indian network before shipping.
(2) The 112.gov.in FAQ is partly copied from a European FAQ. It mentions 'CIC 101', provinces and the EU member list, and it tells callers to 'directly call the emergency number 101 for urgent police assistance' while the About page gives 101 as Fire and Rescue. Do not reuse other FAQ wording without checking it.
(3) The MHA page's line about ERSS 2.0 being expected by March 2026 is out of date. Its 'Last Updated On: 27.10.2026' looks like a footer that shows today's date, so it does not date the content.
(4) How fully 181 and other numbers are integrated with 112 varies by state. newsonair.gov.in (AIR, July 2023) reported child-helpline integration done in only nine states.

research.line: NALSA (National Legal Services Authority) national legal aid helpline
research.official_name: NALSA's name for the line varies between its own pages. They call it "NALSA Helpline Toll-Free Number" (nalsa.gov.in homepage), "National Legal Aid Helpline Number" (newsletter back covers, 2023-24), "Toll-free National Legal Aid Helpline" (Women page) and "National Toll-Free Helpline Number 15100 of NALSA" (Annual Report 2023-24). The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) allotment calls it "Free Legal Service Helpline". The number in every case is 15100. A clean Hindi name could not be pulled: the Hindi text layers in the annual reports came out garbled.
research.run_by: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), the central body set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, housed at the Supreme Court of India, New Delhi. The DoT 2023 letter names it "National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) helpline, Ministry of Law and Justice". Calls go through an automated phone menu (IVRS) to the State and District Legal Services Authorities (SLSA/DLSA): their front offices and panel advocates. The staff user guide for the system, linked from nalsa.gov.in at nalsa15100.in, is labelled "By Team Eurys", which looks like the vendor's name. NALSA pays for the line: Rs 1,65,71,839 in 2024-25 and Rs 92,10,866 in 2023-24.

facts.value: Under Section 12, every woman and child qualifies for free legal aid, whatever their income. A man qualifies only if he falls in a listed group: SC/ST, trafficking victim, person with a disability, disaster victim, industrial workman, person in custody, or annual income under Rs 3 lakh (or the state's own limit). Anyone else can still get free legal advice and assistance.

I re-fetched all 9 numbers and 29 facts myself with curl, and every one is confirmed in raw text I saved. Nothing was contradicted.

How I checked:
- HTML pages were stripped to text. Text-layer PDFs went through pdftotext.
- Three sources were scanned images, so I ran tesseract OCR and also checked them by eye:
  - The 2023 DoT mapping PDF from the Wayback Machine (300 ppi). It encloses the 27/05/2014 allotment letter as page 3.
  - Annexure A-1 of that PDF. I counted 37 rows by eye: Andhra Pradesh 18001806715, Delhi 18001806730, Chandigarh 18001806751, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu as separate rows.
  - The Jan-Jun 2020 newsletter. Its OCR confirms the 7,260 figure.
- The 2026 www.dot.gov.in copy of the 2014 letter is a 72 ppi JPEG that cannot be OCR'd. I only read it by eye. The quoted text comes from the 300 ppi enclosed copy.

Corrections to the other agent's write-up:
- The staff user guide is linked from the nalsa15100.in login page, not directly from nalsa.gov.in.
- On the 2014 letter, OCR reads '15100' as '115100' and '(iii)' as '(ii)'. By eye both are correct in the image.

Hours:
- The automated menu (IVRS) answers 24x7.
- A person (SLSA/DLSA front office or panel advocate) is reached only 10 AM to 5 PM.
- Missed calls get a call-back by the next working day.
- Emergency calls go to the caller's state SLSA. The guide does not say whether this works outside 10 to 5.
- nalsa.gov.in itself states no hours. The '24x7' wording on the help sheet would be accurate only for the automated menu.

Coverage:
- Category-I: every access provider must carry it, and it is unrestricted on STD.
- Mapped to 37 state/UT toll-free numbers.
- Calls are routed by the caller's state and district.
- No text says 'mobile and landline' in so many words.

Serves women and men alike:
- The guide defines a caller as any citizen, and callers can choose a male or female panel advocate.
- Free legal aid itself is unequal: automatic for every woman, category-based for men. Legal advice is open to anyone.

Languages:
- The only official text says '10 Indian languages' for the helpline and names none.
- The 2023 DLSA manual names English, Hindi and 8 others for the LSMS portal and mobile app, not for the helpline. That is only a lead that the helpline uses the same 10.
- It is also a lead that the 'NALSA Legal Services' app (com.nalsa.lsmsapp) is the LSMS app.

Still current:
- The NALSA homepage (last updated 15 October 2026) still lists 15100.
- So does the Apr-Jun 2025 NALSA newsletter.
- No official text I fetched says 15100 changed, merged or closed.

Open question before shipping: whether a call to 15100 can ever be charged. DoT's 'Metered Service' wording has never been withdrawn in any text I found, though it may be outdated. NALSA consistently says toll-free.

fit.chapter_topic: Rukavat (a family home): who the children live with when parents separate (woman's half and man's half)
fit.why: Custody and guardianship are legal questions, and NALSA covers every kind of case. FAQ: "There is hence, no bar as to which kind of cases one can apply and not apply for." (https://nalsa.gov.in/faqs/). NALSA's women's page says a caller to 15100 can "Speak with a Panel Lawyer who will guide you on how to proceed." (https://nalsa.gov.in/womens-assistance/). NALSA also runs mediation, which suits a separation. Adversarial catch: the free LAWYER is unequal by sex. FAQ: "Yes, a woman is entitled for free legal aid irrespective of her income or financial status." A father gets free representation only if he fits another Section 12 category, such as an income below the state ceiling. Free ADVICE is open to everyone (see the quote above), so the line serves both halves. But the sheet must say "free legal advice", not "a free lawyer".

fit.chapter_topic: Rukavat (a family home): a dowry demand for a cousin's wedding (woman's half and man's half)
fit.why: A dowry demand is a crime, and a relative is allowed to act. NALSA's own Women and Law handbook lists "Demanding dowry [Section 4]" with a jail term. It says a complaint can be made "by the person aggrieved by offence or a parent or other relative of such person" (https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s32e45f93088c7db59767efef516b306aa/uploads/2025/04/202504081538695387.pdf, the PDF linked from nalsa.gov.in/women-and-law/). So a cousin of either sex asking "what can we do?" is a legal-advice question, and a legal-aid line fits it better than an emergency or women-only line. Adversarial limit: 15100 is advice and aid, not emergency response. If the demand turns into violence or a threat, the right route is police or emergency services, which this line does not replace. The women-only lines (181, NCW) fail the both-halves rule, so they are not better.

The recommendation is KEEP, but only if these conditions hold before it ships:
(1) Hindi and English are NOT confirmed by any official raw text. The only language claims are non-official leads. India Customer Care, a directory site, gives an IVR menu that starts \"First please select your preferred language\". Kashmir Reader (5 Oct 2024) says it \"operates 24/7 in multiple languages\". The owner should confirm by a test call or by writing to NALSA before shipping. I did not call.
(2) Do not print \"24x7\". NALSA's own pages never say it. The legal-aid page gives NALSA office hours as \"Monday and Friday – from 9:30 am to 6 pm\". The newsonair.gov.in item (30 Aug 2024) quotes a district official saying information about schemes and campaigns is on the number \"24 घंटे\". That covers scheme information, not lawyer advice.
(3) Sheet copy should say \"free legal advice\", not \"free lawyer\". Free representation is unequal by sex: women get it regardless of income, men only under other Section 12 criteria.
(4) Check the numbers: NALSA's own pages disagree on the Section 12(h) income limit. promoting-inclusive-legal-system says \"less than Rs 1,00,000/-\". FAQ 16 says \"less than Rs. 03 lakh\" and Rs 12,000 for the Supreme Court. The legal-aid page has a state table and gives Rs 5 lakh for the Supreme Court. Print no income figure.

Alternative considered and not named as better: Tele-Law 14454 (Department of Justice and CSC; tele-law.in, Last Update 26 Oct 2026). Its FAQ says \"Yes, all citizens are eligible for free legal advice through Tele-Law scheme.\" It lists \"Dowry, family dispute, divorce, protection from domestic violence.\" Its history page says a toll-free number 14454 launched in 2024. It is equal for both sexes, but it is pre-litigation advice by appointment only, with no representation or mediation. Official text about the 14454 phone line itself is thin, and its languages are unverified. doj.gov.in pages are JavaScript-only, and the Rajya Sabha answer PDF redirects to a JavaScript shell, so I could not read either. Tele-Law is a credible fallback if NALSA fails the language check, but it is not clearly better.
